This Writ Petition is filed in the form of a pubic interest litigation seeking the following reliefs:
"A. A writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writ, order or direction commanding respondents to regulate the functioning of catering services in the state under the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Saijo Joseph vs The State Of Kerala on 25 July, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151268998/
2 Businesses) Regulations, 2011.
B. A writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writ, order or direction commanding the respondents to prohibit all catering services functioning or doing business of catering in the state without a license and hygienic and safety requirements as provided under the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011."
2.

entities.text: Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The main complaint of the petitioner is that though caterers also come within the ambit of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the respondent authorities having issued Exhibit P1 circular indicating the necessity for taking of precautionary measures in terms of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, which is applicable only to hotels and restaurants, no such steps have been initiated by the Government as far as the caterers are concerned.

According to the petitioner, there are large number of catering organisations within the State and unless such safety measures are being implemented, there will be no control in respect of the food supplied by such organisations.

3. The learned Government Pleader, on instructions, would submit that necessary steps have already been taken by the respondent authorities to insist for compliance of requirement under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Rules framed thereunder.

As far as the measures are concerned,
necessary instructions are given to them to get licence/permission from the authorities concerned by the end of February, 2014.
4.

Having regard to the fact that a circular in terms of Exhibit P1 dated 25.7.2012 has been issued under the aforesaid Act in the form of guidelines, we are of the view that a similar circular should be issued in respect of caterers also insisting the requirements of taking necessary licences and intimating them the nature of requirements they have to follow for carrying on the catering business.

In the above circumstances, the Writ Petition is disposed of directing the respondent authorities to issue necessary circular applicable to caterers also for compliance of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
This shall be done within one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

MANJULA CHELLUR, CHIEF JUSTICE A.M.SHAFFIQUE, JUDGE vgs5.12 Saijo Joseph vs The State Of Kerala on 25 July, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151268998/
